August 29, 2026

Federal judge blocks Trump bid to move hush money conviction to federal court

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Judge Hellerstein of the Southern District of New York rejected Donald Trump's attempt to move his New York state conviction on 34 felony counts into federal court. Trump had argued the hush money payments to Stormy Daniels amounted to official acts covered by presidential immunity, a route that could have led to dismissal. The judge found no new evidence had been presented to justify removal, leaving the state conviction intact.

Texas suspends 1.2 million voters from the rolls weeks before November elections

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

The Texas Secretary of State has suspended roughly 1.2 million voters from the state's voter rolls days before early voting begins for the November elections, with affected voters reportedly not directly notified. Officials attribute the suspensions to outdated registration records, and the change affects Republicans, Democrats and independents alike. Voters have until October 5 to update their registration status, and can check their status at votetexas.gov using a driver's license or ID card, Social Security number, and voter unique identifier.

Seventh Circuit rules private possession of AI-generated child sexual abuse imagery is protected speech

tags: legal, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

The Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of possession charges against Steven Anderec, who used the AI image generator Stable Diffusion to create hundreds of photorealistic sexual images of minors and was caught after sending one to a child on Instagram. The court held it was bound by Stanley v. Georgia (1969), which bars prosecution for private possession of obscene material in the home, and Ashcroft v. Free Speech Coalition (2002), which found images merely resembling CSAM to be protected speech. Government arguments about grooming and normalization of abuse had already been rejected by the Supreme Court in 2002. The appeals court issued a warning that addressing the gap is a matter for lawmakers, noting the absence of AI regulation.

Trump Interior Department pushes road through Yosemite for private developer

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich, @aaronparnas

A Las Vegas firm, Kingsbarn Realty Capital, bought two 40-acre parcels near Yosemite National Park for $4 million in 2024 through a company called Sanctuary at Yosemite, and wants a road across park land that would cut a roughly 90-minute drive to Yosemite Valley into a shortcut. The property sits about five miles from the Mariposa Grove of giant sequoias; the previous owner sought the same road in the early 2000s and was refused by the Park Service, a decision upheld in federal court. Sources told NOTUS that Interior officials are pressuring park staff to move faster, and the New York Times reported Interior told Congress it may fund the swap using the Land and Water Conservation Fund. Interior says no final decision has been made, that there has been no political pressure, and that any exchange would undergo environmental review and public notice with land of equal value in return.

FBI loosens hiring standards on bestiality, prostitution and theft

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The FBI has relaxed its hiring standards amid staff losses, under a directive issued by Director Kash Patel earlier this year and first reported by CBS. Bestiality or animal cruelty committed before the age of 18 is no longer an automatic disqualifier, applicants who paid for sex may be considered if it occurred fewer than three times and at least 10 years ago, and theft from an employer more than three years ago is no longer an automatic bar. Applicants may still be barred on other grounds.

Milo Yiannopoulos detained by ICE in Louisiana

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Milo Yiannopoulos, a right-wing commentator who served as Kanye West's chief of staff for nearly two years before leaving in 2024, has been detained by ICE, according to TMZ. He was taken into custody at an airport and is being held at a detention facility in Louisiana. The circumstances of the detention are not yet clear.

Florida deputy of the year resigns after using Flock cameras to track ex-girlfriend

tags: surveillance, policing
sources: @aaronparnas

Michael Foltz, named Florida Deputy of the Year, has resigned from the Brevard County sheriff's office following misconduct allegations. According to News 6, he used Flock automated license plate reader cameras to track his ex-girlfriend and bragged about it to her, logging the reason for the searches as "investigation." He is also alleged to have posed for photographs dressed as Adolf Hitler, taken pictures of his ex-girlfriend with his service weapon in her mouth, and used racial slurs in text messages. Foltz denies using Flock to stalk her. 404 Media has reported the case as part of a broader pattern of misuse.

Ted Cruz says he urged Trump to strike Iran

tags: politics, war
sources: @ericmoutsos

In an interview, Senator Ted Cruz said he personally urged President Trump to launch the strikes on Iran, describing spending the day before the attack with him aboard Air Force One and one-on-one in the presidential limousine discussing what to do. Cruz said he argued the regime was weaker than ever and that its collapse would do more for American national security than almost anything else. In separate remarks to Tucker Carlson, Cruz said he entered Congress intending to be the leading defender of Israel in the Senate and grounded his support in scripture, though he was unable to cite the passage when pressed.

Saudi money and Trump family entities dominate World Liberty crypto venture

tags: politics, markets
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Leaked reporting indicates Saudi Arabia accounts for roughly 50% of the investment backing Trump's crypto venture, World Liberty. A further 38% of incoming investment is said to be tied to family connections, and an entity related to the Trump family personally holds about 39% of ownership. The arrangement raises conflict of interest concerns about the president benefiting financially from foreign dealings while in office.

Justice Department sues 21 states over in-state tuition for undocumented students

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Justice Department has filed suit against 21 states over policies granting in-state tuition rates to undocumented students. The action is part of a broader wave of federal moves reported the same day, alongside a Trump announcement of the largest oil deal with Venezuela in American history for which the destination of funds is unclear, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reportedly weighing a presidential run.

Trump cabinet secretaries confronted by voters on economic messaging tour

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Cabinet secretaries dispatched across the country by Trump and Susie Wiles to promote the administration's economic messaging have been repeatedly confronted by members of the public, according to Politico. Energy Secretary Chris Wright faced complaints about gas prices, Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins was pressed in Iowa on beef prices and the sourcing of imported beef, and Health Secretary RFK Jr. was challenged over the ongoing measles outbreak in Florida. The tour was intended to boost the president's favourability numbers. Separately, the Federal Reserve chairman has described inflation as concerning.

Trump signs order creating U.S. Space Academy modelled on West Point

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Trump signed an order beginning the creation of a U.S. Space Academy, modelled after the West Point military academy. Graduates could face a military service requirement.

Army tests self-driving F-250 with shotgun turret for drone defence

tags: defence, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

The U.S. Army has tested a self-driving Ford F-250 fitted with a shotgun turret designed to shoot down drones. The vehicle is part of counter-drone development work.

Air Force declines to commit to investigation of $800 million dorm failures

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Dormitories built at a cost of $800 million failed after just 16 years, forcing more than 5,000 troops to move out. The Air Force has not ordered an investigation into the failures and has declined to commit to one.

Army tests AI suicide-risk screening after study finds soldiers denied symptoms

tags: health, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

An Army study found that 95% of later suicide attempts followed soldiers denying suicidal thoughts on their Periodic Health Assessment. In response, the Army is testing an AI-based suicide-risk detection system.

Navy investigation finds stored toilet paper worsened $12 million ship fire

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

A Navy investigation into a $12 million fire aboard the USS New Orleans found that roughly 100 boxes of toilet paper obstructed the ship's sprinkler system. The obstruction contributed to the severity of the blaze.

Recalls issued for frozen buffalo chicken and packaged white rice

tags: health
sources: @aaronparnas

Nearly 25,000 pounds of frozen buffalo chicken and more than 27,000 packages of white rice have been recalled in the United States. The chicken, produced by Shanghai Ravioli Company without the benefit of inspection, is subject to a Class I recall indicating a potentially fatal health hazard; it covers not-ready-to-eat buffalo chicken with sell-by dates from July 8, 2026 to June 19, 2027 and buffalo chicken mozzarella sticks from July 8, 2026 to June 29, 2027, distributed in Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island and Vermont. The rice, from Lundberg Family Farms, was sold in 32-ounce packages under UPC 073416040281 in Florida, North Carolina, Tennessee and other states.

Ottawa council moves to strip Trump's name from residential street

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Ottawa City Council voted unanimously to begin the process of renaming Trump Avenue, a residential street in the Central Park neighbourhood that has carried the name for about 25 years. The move follows Trump renaming Lake Ontario. Names under consideration include Taco Avenue, Obama Avenue, Pelosi Avenue, Gulf of Mexico Avenue, Canada Goose Avenue, Ontario Avenue and Rosie O'Donnell Avenue.
